children: U.S. stock futures fell into negative territory late Tuesday as euphoria over Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) faded, and Anthropic (ANT) shares fell below their listing price, putting pressure on the technology sector.
Meanwhile, markets are awaiting October’s U.S. Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE), the Fed’s preferred gauge for inflation, which is scheduled for release on Wednesday.
As of 9:51 p.m. EST, Dow futures fell 0.33%, while the S&P 500 futures declined 0.65% and Nasdaq-100 futures dropped 1.17%.

On Tuesday, the three U.S. benchmark indexes closed mixed. The Nasdaq Composite shed 356 points to close 1.48% lower, while the S&P 500 declined 0.50%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed 0.85% higher.

Technology Trade Weakens After Monday’s Rally
U.S. stock markets closed another volatile session on Tuesday as technology stocks sold off amid declines in NVDA and ANT shares after a massive rally the day before.

lost more than 7%.
Huang’s return seems to have provided a temporary leg up to markets, which then corrected amid lingering concerns about the AI trade and inflation.
The Kobeissi Letter noted in a post on X that inflation remains America’s biggest concern, as prices have been surging amid the Iran war and other economic pressures.
The market commentator said that 40% of U.S. consumers expect their financial situation to deteriorate over the next 12 months, the second-highest reading on record.
The October U.S. Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE), the Fed’s preferred gauge for inflation, scheduled for release on Wednesday, is likely to provide more cues on the economy.
Analysts expect the U.S. October headline PCE price index to rise 3.8% year-over-year and core PCE to increase 0.3% month-over-month, according to a Bloomberg survey.

The data comes ahead of the Federal Reserve’s December policy meeting, where it is widely expected to hike interest rates. Data from the CME FedWatch tool puts the probability of a 25 bps rate hike in December at 96.4%, while the odds of a 50 bps hike are at 3.6%.
However, market experts are split on what the decision should be, with Ed Yardeni, economist and president of Yardeni Research,
that the market reversal following Huang’s return may be a “one-day wonder” and that he believes the Fed should hike rates by 50 bps.

Meanwhile, James E. Thorne, Chief Market Strategist at Wellington Altus, believes that Huang’s reinstatement and falling energy prices have brought some stability to markets, and is championing for the central bank to cut rates in 2027.
Market Risks
Mohamed El-Erian, Chief Economic Advisor at Allianz, noted in a post on X that the market is providing “warning signals, especially with respect to technicals,” that have extended well beyond Nvidia.
“The key question now is whether bad technicals risk becoming back fundamentals,” he said.

Meanwhile, Jurrien Timmer, Director of Global Macro at Fidelity Investments, said in a post on X, “The S&P 500 index is now down 12.3% from its intraday high set on October 6th. That ranks as a garden-variety correction in the grand scheme of things, although it feels worse than that in real time (it always does). History shows that the market is in a 10% drawdown about half the time, or every other year. And bear markets occur every 4-5 years. The last major corrections were a year and a half ago (Tariff Tantrum) and four years ago (the Rate Reset).”

However, The Kobeissi Letter believes that market corrections are a regular phenomenon. It noted in a post on X that the U.S. equity market has averaged one correction of 10%+ per year since 1930. Since 2000, the S&P 500 has seen 24 regular corrections, it said.

“Despite these declines, the S&P 500 has delivered positive annual returns in 19 calendar years since 2000. Furthermore, US stocks have posted 3.4 pullbacks of 5%+ per year on average since 1930. By comparison, a bear market has occurred once every 3.3 years on average over the same period,” it said.
Rising Tensions In The Middle East

While oil prices have retreated from their recent highs, with Brent crude futures trading at $90.25 a barrel, down 1.28% at the time of writing, and WTI crude futures trading 1.45% lower at $80.86 per barrel, concerns remain about the ongoing conflict with Iran.

The Trump administration is considering whether the U.S. military should target top Iranian leaders, according to a U.S. official and a person with knowledge of the discussions, NBC News reported on Tuesday.
Tensions in the Strait of Hormuz continue to escalate, with reports that Iran-backed Houthis attacked a Saudi-led coalition in Yemen’s Hodeidah port.

“The reality on the ground is more a ‘war but no war’ situation, with spasms of violence,” Robert Yawger, director of the energy futures division at Mizuho Securities USA LLC, told Bloomberg. Under those circumstances, “look for the supply surplus to become the dominant theme in coming weeks,” he said.
Precious Metals Sentiment Drops
Meanwhile, gold and silver prices have been tumbling amid the ongoing market volatility. Spot gold prices were trading at $3,556.56 an ounce at the time of writing, while spot silver fell to $40.81.
The Kobeissi Letter said in a post on X that global physical gold-backed exchange-traded funds posted 20 tonnes of gold outflows last week, their largest weekly withdrawal since June.

“Last week's outflows were driven by the US's largest gold-backed ETF, $GLD, which recorded -10 tonnes in withdrawals. US outflows totalled -12 tonnes, followed by China and the UK, both at 3 tonnes,” it said, adding that global gold ETFs are now on track for their first monthly outflow in 5 months, and only their third in 2026.
“Sentiment in precious metals markets has become extremely pessimistic,” it said.
Trending Tickers To Watch
Dell Technologies Inc. (DELL):
Shares slumped nearly 12% at close on Tuesday amid the tech selloff and fell further overnight despite reporting a blockbuster fiscal third quarter that more than doubled revenue.
Ambarella Inc. (AMBA):

The chip company plunged more than 37% overnight after reporting a double miss in its third-quarter print and issuing fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $70.0 million to $75.0 million, below Street expectations.
Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X Shares (SOXL):

The leveraged exchange-traded fund that aims to deliver 300% of the daily performance of an underlying semiconductor index was in focus amid the drawdown in technology shares. It slumped nearly 8% overnight.
Strategy (MSTR):
The company was in focus after its shares slumped to a 52-week low in regular trading hours on Tuesday as a slide in Bitcoin prices weighed on the company.
Other Market Trends

Among ETFs tracking benchmark indexes, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) was down 0.74% in the overnight session at the time of writing, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) fell 1.29% and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) edged 0.33% higher.
The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield was trading at 4.902%, while the 30-year yield was at 5.298%.
The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) was up 0.18% amid ‘bullish’ sentiment.
Asian markets opened lower on Wednesday. South Korea's KOSPI, China’s SSE Composite index, Japan’s Nikkei 225 and Australian stocks all traded in the red at the open.
The Kobeissi Letter noted in a post on X that inflation remains America’s biggest concern as prices have been surging amid the Iran war and other pressures on the economy.
The October U.S. Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE), the Fed’s preferred gauge of inflation, is scheduled for release on Wednesday and is likely to provide more cues on the economy.
The data comes ahead of the Federal Reserve’s December policy meeting, where it is widely expected to hike interest rates.

title: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq Futures Edge Lower Amid Tech Selloff Ahead Of Key Inflation Data: DELL, AMBA, SOXL, MSTR In Focus
